items.content:
GS네오텍이 아마존웹서비스(AWS)의 'AWS Agentic AI 컴피턴시'를 취득했다고 밝혔다. 이번 취득으로 기존 '생성형 AI 컴피턴시'에 이어 에이전틱 AI 분야까지 AWS 공인 전문성을 확보했다.

AWS AI 컴피턴시의 'Agentic AI 컨설팅 서비스' 부문은 상황을 스스로 이해하고 목표에 따라 자율 추론하며 사람의 개입을 최소화해 실행을 완수하는 엔터프라이즈급 AI 솔루션 파트너를 인증하는 자격이다. 비즈니스 정합성과 거버넌스 요건을 충족하는 동시에 복잡한 배포 과정을 해결하는 전략 수립부터 실질적 구현, 지속적 지원 역량을 평가한다.

GS네오텍은 이번 심사에서 AI 프로젝트 착수 방법론, 파운데이션 모델 선정 기준, 데이터 보안 및 컴플라이언스 체계, 책임 있는 AI 절차, 운영 전환 및 사후 지원 체계의 표준 프로세스 역량을 입증했다.

기술 역량 평가는 추론, SDK 및 프레임워크, 상호운용성, 보안, 책임 있는 AI, 컴퓨팅의 6개 영역에 걸쳐 진행됐다. 아마존 베드록 및 아마존 세이지메이커 AI 기반 모델 활용, 에이전트 프레임워크 구현, MCP와 A2A 프로토콜을 활용한 협업과 외부 도구 연계 기술력을 인정받았다. 아울러 IAM, 베드록 가드레일, SSO 연계를 통한 보안 및 관측 체계와 관리형 컴퓨팅 배포 역량을 두루 평가받았다.

이번 인증을 계기로 GS네오텍은 단순 질의응답 중심의 생성형 AI를 넘어 복잡한 비즈니스 목표를 세부 작업으로 분해하고 ERP와 CRM 등 기간계 시스템과 연동해 실무를 자율 수행하는 프로덕션 수준의 AI 에이전트 구축에 나선다. 클라우드 관리형 서비스 노하우를 접목해 권한 관리, 실행 이력 감사, 비용 최적화, 장애 대응을 아우르는 에이전트 운영 서비스 체계를 가동한다.

미디어와 게임, 제조, 유통 및 리테일, 에너지 산업군을 중심으로 고객 상담 자동화, 사내 지식 검색, IT 운영 자동화 등 업무 특화형 AI 에이전트 레퍼런스를 확대한다. 도입 전략 컨설팅부터 아마존 베드록 에이전트코어 기반 구축, 통합 운영 및 관제에 이르는 엔드 투 엔드 라인업으로 서비스를 고도화한다.

서정인 GS네오텍 IT사업본부장은 "에이전틱 AI가 기업의 일하는 방식을 혁신하는 기술이지만 비즈니스 성과로 이어지려면 보안, 권한 관리, 책임 있는 AI 설계가 전제되어야 한다"며 "공인받은 기술 방법론과 클라우드 운영 노하우를 결합해 기업들이 AI 에이전트를 안정적으로 도입하도록 지원하겠다"고 밝혔다.

items.content:
미국 사이버보안·인프라보안국(CISA)이 브로드컴(Broadcom)의 가상화 플랫폼 브이엠웨어(VMware) ESXi에서 발견된 로그 기록 우회 취약점이 실제 사이버공격에 악용된 사실을 확인하고 긴급 대응을 요구했다. 중국 연계 해커조직이 이 취약점을 이용해 가상화 서버에서 수행한 악성 행위의 흔적을 숨긴 것으로 분석됐다.

CISA는 10월 28일 VMware ESXi의 로그 기록 미흡 취약점인 CVE-2026-41709를 실제 악용 취약점 목록(KEV)에 추가했다. 미국 연방 민간기관에는 11월 11일까지 보안 조치를 완료하도록 요구했다.

글로벌 보안기업 크라우드스트라이크(CrowdStrike)는 10월 28일 발표한 사이버위협 보고서에서 중국 연계 해커조직 워프 판다(Warp Panda)가 해당 취약점을 제로데이 상태에서 악용한 사실을 공개했다.

크라우드스트라이크에 따르면 워프 판다는 미국 법률 분야 조직 등을 대상으로 공격을 수행했으며, 침해한 VMware vCenter 환경에 여러 악성코드를 배포했다.

특히 공격자는 당시 보안 패치가 공개되지 않았던 CVE-2026-41709를 악용해 가상화 시스템에서 수행한 특정 작업이 로그에 남지 않도록 한 것으로 분석됐다.

해당 취약점은 지난 7월 29일 공식 공개됐으며, 공격은 그 이전부터 발생한 것으로 조사됐다. 다만 공격자가 최초로 관리자 권한을 확보한 구체적인 침입 경로는 공개되지 않았다.

이번 취약점은 공통취약점평가시스템(CVSS) 3.1 기준 2.7점으로 낮은 위험등급에 해당한다.

관리자 수준의 높은 권한이 있어야 악용할 수 있기 때문이다. 그러나 공격자가 이미 관리자 계정을 탈취한 상황이라면 시스템에서 수행한 일부 악성 작업의 기록을 남기지 않아 보안 담당자의 추적을 어렵게 만들 수 있다.

특히 VMware ESXi는 기업의 주요 업무시스템과 데이터베이스, 인증 서버 등을 가상머신으로 운영하는 핵심 인프라다. 공격자가 가상화 관리 환경을 장악하면 여러 업무시스템에 영향을 미칠 수 있다.

브로드컴은 해당 취약점을 포함한 VMware 보안 취약점에 대한 수정 버전을 배포했다. 영향을 받는 제품에는 VMware ESXi 8.0과 9.0·9.1 계열, VMware Cloud Foundation 등이 포함된다.

국내 VMware 기반 가상화 환경을 운영하는 금융기관과 공공기관, 기업들도 보안 점검이 필요하다.

우선 ESXi와 vCenter의 보안 업데이트 적용 여부를 확인하고, 관리자 계정에 대한 다중요소인증(MFA)과 관리 인터페이스 접근통제를 강화해야 한다.

특히 이번 취약점처럼 시스템 내부에 로그가 남지 않는 상황에 대비해 중앙 로그 관리시스템과 외부 인증시스템, 네트워크 보안장비의 기록을 함께 점검할 필요가 있다.

items.content:
TeamViewer has fixed a flaw that lets the machine being controlled in a remote session attack the computer that connected to control it. In a TeamViewer session, the computer that connects and takes control is the viewer, and the machine it controls is the host.

A malicious or compromised host can exploit the flaw to crash the viewer's TeamViewer and, depending on the platform, may also run code on the viewer's computer. This works only after the user starts a remote-control session to that host. The fix is in TeamViewer version 15.83.

The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-111585 and scored 8.8 out of 10, in the high range. It affects the TeamViewer Full Client on Windows, Linux, and macOS, the Windows Portable edition, and the Android Remote Control app, in all versions before 15.83.

For this flaw, TeamViewer's bulletin lists the Full Client, Portable, and Android app, but not the Host. The same 15.83 update fixes two other flaws in that bulletin that do affect the Host, so people running the Host should update as well.

Omri Dar, a researcher at security firm Remedio, published a technical account of the flaw on October 29. In this bug, he wrote, "the attacker is the host and the victim is the viewer."

In a remote session, the host tells the viewer how large its screen image is. The viewer uses that size to set aside memory, but the calculation can overflow and reserve too little. Screen data that arrives afterward is then written past the end of that space.

At a minimum, this crashes the viewer's TeamViewer session, and the host can trigger the crash again whenever they want.

On Windows, Remedio says it took the bug further, bypassing the operating system's built-in exploit defenses and running code of its choosing in the viewer. The demonstration used a stand-in on the host to supply part of the attack data, so it is not yet an attack carried out entirely over the network.

That result was shown only on Windows. Whether the same works on macOS, Linux, or Android is not covered in the write-up. TeamViewer only says that code execution is possible, depending on the platform.

The attack needs no password and no extra click beyond accepting the session, and it works in TeamViewer's default setup, Dar wrote. The flaw affects all versions before 15.83, including 15.82, the security update TeamViewer released in September . Updating last month did not remove it.

The only fix TeamViewer offers is to update, and it lists no workaround. Current users should move to 15.83 or later. The fixed builds for older supported branches are in the table above.

The same 15.83 update also fixes two other high-severity flaws in the same bulletin, including a separate code-execution flaw affecting Linux and macOS. A companion bulletin the same day, TV-2026-1012, fixes six more flaws in TeamViewer's Remote Management add-ons, delivered by automatic update.

TeamViewer said that when it published the fix, it was unaware of any attacks exploiting the flaw. The vulnerability is not in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of its October 29 listing. Remedio reported no attacks in the wild and did not release exploit code.

items.title: PHP2Shell Attacks Root Palo Alto Firewalls but Fail Against WordPress
items.summary: Over 22.6 million exposed instances are potentially affected by the critical PHP flaws that have been targeted for over a week. The post PHP2Shell Attacks Root Palo Alto Firewalls but Fail Against WordPress appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
Threat actors have been hammering servers vulnerable to PHP2Shell for over a week, but only a few successful compromises have been confirmed to date.

Standing out are Palo Alto Networks firewalls, which have been rooted by a China-linked hacking group in attacks chaining PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia kernel privilege escalation bug.

Assisted by AI, the hackers chained two separate exploits: one specifically targeting the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 on Palo Alto Networks’ PAN-OS devices, and another one for Fragnesia to deploy webshells with root privileges.

Cybersecurity outfit Dream flagged the campaign earlier this week, noting that at least 25 firewalls out of a pool of hundreds were hacked. Palo Alto Networks has since confirmed the findings.

“Dream Research has reported a campaign in which attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation vulnerability to gain root access. Unit 42 has independently verified the same attacker’s tooling and confirmed the reported results,” Palo Alto Networks said .

The company has rolled out patches that resolve the PHP2Shell flaws in PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1, and 10.2 for PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls, and for Panorama (virtual and M-Series). Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

“No special configuration is required to be affected by this issue. Active exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet,” the company notes in its advisory .

Palo Alto Networks says that by default the management interface is not exposed to the internet and urges customers to immediately restrict access to it and apply the available fixes.

“Only a small fraction of a percent (approximately .02%) of our global installed base has internet-facing management interfaces configured and was impacted. Each of these customers has been individually contacted by our teams. We will continue to investigate and provide any necessary updates as they become available,” Palo Alto Networks notes.

According to the company, as of October 29, its telemetry has identified over 22.6 million exposed PHP instances that are potentially vulnerable to the PHP2Shell bugs.

That is not surprising, given that PHP is widely used across servers and content management systems, including WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and many others.

The mass PHP2Shell exploitation has been targeting those as well, but remained largely unsuccessful, at least when it comes to WordPress, web security firm Defiant says .

As of October 28, it was not aware of any WordPress site being compromised via PHP2Shell exploitation, although it has recorded over 77,000 related requests from more than 2,000 IP addresses.

However, Defiant points out that testing has revealed the exploits often need to be adjusted to work on targeted servers, influenced by ASLR, PHP build, running extensions, memory limits, and the server’s request handling.

“Attackers are still changing their tools. A successful attack could give them access to your site’s files, database, and passwords, so updating PHP remains essential,” Defiant warned.

Despite the broad PHP2Shell exploitation attempts, success has been attributed to very few threat actors.

According to Cato Networks , roughly 96% of the attacks it has blocked targeted CVE-2026-109618, and 41% of them attempted remote code execution (RCE), while the remaining were scanning or invalid PoC attempts.

The attempts originated from a handful of IPs in the US, the Netherlands, and Germany, repeating proof-of-concept (PoC) style requests. Most of them focused on command execution, followed by deserialization attempts.

According to Cato, healthcare organizations were targeted the most, followed by technology and security services, professional services, automotive, education and non-profit, and manufacturing, construction, and retail.

items.summary: Noteworthy stories that might have slipped under the radar: Iran eyed in military freezer hacks, Copenhagen University breach, AI-powered malware. The post In Other News: Anthropic Breach Dispute, UEFI Flaw Hits Most Servers, Cloudflare AI Data Leak appeared first on SecurityWeek
items.content:
SecurityWeek’s weekly cybersecurity news roundup offers a concise overview of important developments that may not receive full standalone coverage yet remain relevant to the broader threat landscape.

This curated summary highlights key stories across vulnerability disclosures, emerging attack methods, policy updates, industry reports, and other noteworthy events to help readers stay well-informed about the evolving cybersecurity environment.

Iran suspected in US military freezer hacks

US officials suspect Iran-linked hackers caused freezer malfunctions that spoiled food at around six military base commissaries starting in late August, Nextgov reports, citing people familiar with the matter. At Fort Huachuca in Arizona, a freezer entered defrost mode and heated its contents, and Cyber Command and Defense Department law enforcement units are investigating with French authorities, after hackers overrode refrigeration controls at some 350 French establishments earlier this month.

Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Most servers rely on UEFI code hit by critical boot flaw

A critical 16-year-old buffer overflow (CVE-2026-97631) in TianoCore EDK II, open source code that most of the world’s server vendors and data centers use through firmware suppliers such as AMI, Insyde and Phoenix, means the flaw affects most servers worldwide, Ars Technica reports. An attacker with local network access can send an oversized ICMP error message to a machine while it boots over the network (PXE) to hang the process or, if the target’s firmware build is known, run code at the highest privilege level before defenses such as Secure Boot take effect. Only machines that use network boot are exposed, and the flaw, found by Anthropic and Google researchers, became public months ahead of a planned January disclosure after AMI published a code fix, leaving organizations to seek firmware updates from their vendors.

Anthropic disputes scope of ex-DOGE startup’s AI-led intrusion

Cathedral, a cybersecurity startup founded by former DOGE staffers, says its AI agents found ways into Anthropic’s internal systems in less than 12 hours by abusing weaknesses in third-party business software, reaching meeting transcripts, salary and job offer data, and Slack discussions about the company’s most advanced models, according to a draft report reviewed by the Washington Post (paywalled). Anthropic, which received the findings through its bug bounty program, says only a limited set of sales, HR and IT systems was reached, that it cut off the startup’s access the same day, and that Claude conversations, source code and model weights were not affected. It also accuses Cathedral of breaking the bounty program’s rules by not disclosing all of its activity.

Midterm spending disclosures stall after FEC intrusion attempt

The US Federal Election Commission took its electronic filing system offline after someone attempted to breach its systems , according to an internal FEC email seen by Reuters, leaving political groups unable to submit campaign finance reports a week before the November 3 midterm elections. The outage blocked the 24-hour and 48-hour reports that track last-minute spending on specific races, although past filings remained searchable. The system was restored on October 28.

Hackers obtain national ID numbers, card PINs in University of Copenhagen breach

The University of Copenhagen says hackers who gained access to one of its test environments obtained personal data on about 525,000 current and former members of the university community, including names, phone numbers and personal email addresses, along with national identity (CPR) numbers for many of them. The attack was detected on October 20 and contained, but the PIN codes for the ID cards of roughly 20,000 staff and students were also compromised and have since been reissued. The university says it does not yet know who is behind the attack or what the motive was.

items.content:
Malicious Claude Code extension on Cursor planted SSH backdoors

A malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension was distributed through Cursor's extension marketplace for approximately 11 hours on October 29, exposing up to 5,000 developers to malware designed to install persistent SSH backdoors.

The extension used the version number 2.1.313 and was distributed between 2:27 a.m. and 1:35 p.m. Pacific Time.

Cursor is an AI-powered code editor built from Microsoft’s open-source Visual Studio Code (VS Code), with support for VS Code extensions. Anthropic’s Claude Code extension brings its AI coding assistant directly into compatible editors, helping developers write and debug code using natural-language instructions.

Cursor says Anthropic did not develop the malicious extension but has not explained how attackers distributed the compromised package under Anthropic's name.

"Between about 2:27 am PT and 1:35 pm PT today, a maliciously modified version of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension was made available in the Cursor VS Code extension Marketplace," warned Cursor .

"The extension runs malicious code that attempts to install a persistent SSH backdoor."

Researchers at Phorion and OpenSourceMalware found that the attackers inserted a malicious JavaScript loader at the beginning of the extension's extension.js file, leaving the legitimate extension code otherwise unchanged.

The malicious code executes when the extension loads, without requiring user interaction with Claude Code.

When installed, the malicious extension performs the following actions on compromised systems:

Collects system and user information, including Git email and public IP address.

Adds an attacker-controlled SSH key and attempts to enable SSH access and establish a reverse tunnel.

Installs persistence through a macOS LaunchAgent or Windows scheduled task/Startup script, retrying the tunnel roughly every minute.

Sends host details and backdoor status to the attacker’s server at the IP address 134.209.82[.]225

However, according to Phorion, coding errors in the malware's SSH setup routines likely prevented attackers from gaining remote access to many affected Windows and macOS systems.

The mistakes prevented the malware from enabling SSH on machines where it was not already running, leaving the reverse tunnel unable to provide access to the compromised device.

On macOS, the malware attempts to check whether Remote Login is enabled using the systemsetup -getremotelogin command, but runs it without elevated privileges. Instead of returning the SSH service's status, the command produces an administrator-access error.

Because the malware only attempts to enable SSH when the output contains "Off," it skips the activation step entirely.

On Windows, the malware attempts to install and start the OpenSSH server through PowerShell, but it tries to do so via /bin/sh, a Unix shell that isn't available on standard Windows installations. Due to this, the SSH setup fails.

In both cases, the malware can still install its SSH keys, establish persistence, and attempt to create the reverse tunnel. However, if the SSH server is not already running, the tunnel cannot provide access to the compromised machine.

Even if the SSH backdoor fails, the malware still sends reconnaissance data to the attacker's server, including the victim's username, hostname, public IP address, Git email address, and names of environment variables associated with sensitive credentials.

However, the script does not directly steal credentials, suggesting the attackers intended to retrieve sensitive data manually after gaining access through the SSH tunnel.

Cursor removed the malicious extension and temporarily shut down its entire marketplace to audit other extensions and rotate all access keys before making it available again.

items.title: Syrian Electronic Army hacker gets prison time for attacks on Western targets
items.summary: Ahmad Umar Agha, known online as “Th3Pr0,” was sentenced Thursday in federal court in Virginia to 42 months behind bars for his role in a conspiracy that was organized by former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's closest advisers.
items.content:
Image: FBI Syrian Electronic Army hacker gets prison time for attacks on Western targets

A prolific hacker with the Syrian Electronic Army was sentenced to more than three years in prison for carrying out cyber campaigns against nearly 50 Western targets, the Justice Department announced this week.

Ahmad Umar Agha, known online as “Th3Pr0,” was sentenced Thursday in federal court in Virginia to 42 months behind bars for his role in a conspiracy that was organized by former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's closest advisers.

The hacking group has been involved since at least 2011 in computer intrusions in support of Assad, whose government was eventually overthrown by a rebel coalition in 2024 after a protracted civil war.

In one notable 2013 incident, the group said it hijacked the Associated Press’s Twitter account and sent out a tweet that falsely reported an explosion at the White House had injured President Barack Obama. The hoax caused a brief $136 billion dip in the stock market.

A 2014 FBI affidavit said that Twitter's message confirming a password reset for the account was sent to an email address used by Agha.

In another attack, Agha gained access to a company hosting the Marine Corps’ recruiting website and redirected visitors to a propaganda message that urged service members to disobey orders and join the Syrian Army.

The U.S. first charged Agha for his criminal activities in 2014. In 2016, the FBI added him and another member of the Syrian Electronic Army, Firas Dardar, to its Cyber's Most Wanted list with a $100,000 reward.

Both men were indicted by a federal grand jury in 2018. Agha was taken into U.S. custody last year, however the DOJ has not given details of his arrest. Dardar remains a fugitive.

All together, Agha hacked about 47 Western media outlets, non-profit groups and other entities allied with the U.S., according to the DOJ.

The department also said the group’s digital conspiracy collected intelligence for Assad’s government before its fall.

"Agha deployed his hacking skills in the service of Assad's regime to silence reporting on the regime's atrocities, intimidate its opponents, and incite U.S. servicemembers to refuse their orders," John Eisenberg, assistant attorney general for national security, said in a statement.

items.content:
인공지능(AI)과 디지털 전환이 산업현장 전반으로 확산하면서 국가기반시설과 스마트공장의 사이버물리시스템(CPS), 운영기술(OT), 산업제어시스템(ICS)의 안전한 운영을 위한 보안 전략을 논의하는 자리가 마련된다.

K-ICS 협의회와 데일리시큐가 주최하고 앤앤에스피(NNSP)가 주관하는 ‘CPS(OT/ICS) Secure AX Summit 2026’이 오는 11월 13일(금) 오전 11시 20분부터 오후 5시까지 서울 양재 엘타워 2층 안단테홀에서 개최된다. 한국기계전기전자시험연구원(KTC)과 호서대학교가 후원한다. 참석 대상은 공공 및 기업의 OT/ICS 보안 담당자다.

이번 행사는 ‘AX 시대, 산업현장의 안전한 연결과 안정적 운영을 위한 기술·대응 전략’을 주제로, 산업제어시스템의 최신 사이버 위협과 국가 보안 정책, 제어망 보호 기술, 제조기업의 실제 보안 구축 및 운영 사례를 공유하기 위해 마련됐다.

특히 산업현장의 AI 활용과 IT·OT 환경 간 연결이 확대되는 상황에서 제어시스템의 가용성과 안정성을 유지하면서 보안 수준을 높일 수 있는 실질적인 대응 방안에 초점을 맞췄다.

행사는 오전 11시 20분 참가자 등록을 시작으로 점심 식사와 네트워킹이 진행되며, 오후 1시부터 본격적인 발표가 시작된다.

첫 번째 초청강연에서는 김수득 컨설턴트가 ‘CPS(OT/ICS) 위협 동향과 국가·기반시설 보안 정책 대응 전략’을 주제로 산업제어시스템의 사이버 위협과 정책적 대응 방향을 소개한다.

앤앤에스피 김기현 최고기술책임자(CTO)는 ‘지속가능한 자율운용 OT 제어망 보안 통합 전략’을 주제로 제어망 보안 모니터링 구축 사례와 안정적인 운영을 위한 통합 보안 전략을 발표한다.

앤앤에스피 송재은 본부장은 ‘AI 시대 OT 망분리·연계 보안의 완성: 차세대 CDS(Cross Domain Security) 기술 소개’를 통해 서로 다른 보안 영역 간 안전한 데이터 연계와 제어망 보호 기술을 설명할 예정이다.

오후 세션에서는 산업현장에 적용할 수 있는 구체적인 보안 기술과 운영 사례가 소개된다.

‘RAPIEnet 프로토콜 모니터링 기반 제어망 위협 대응 체계’를 주제로 산업용 통신 프로토콜에 대한 보안 모니터링과 위협 대응 방안을 다룬다.

KTC 제어시스템 평가·검증 기술을 소개하는 세션과 함께 이병권 컨설턴트가 국제 산업자동화·제어시스템 보안 표준인 IEC 62443에 대한 제조기업의 대응 방안을 설명한다.

황인구 최고정보보호책임자(CISO)는 ‘제조기업의 OT 보안 운영 사례’를 주제로 실제 산업현장에서의 보안 운영 경험을 공유한다.

마지막 기술 세션에서는 앤앤에스피 박혜용 연구소장이 산업용 네트워크 가시성 확보와 위협 탐지 기술을 소개하고, nNetCDS·nNetNDR·nNetHealth 솔루션을 활용한 라이브 시연을 진행한다.

참석자들은 제어망의 통신 현황을 파악하고 이상행위를 탐지하는 기술을 직접 확인할 수 있다.

이번 행사는 무료 사전등록제로 운영되며, 사전등록 마감일은 11월 10일(화)이다.

좌석이 한정된 관계로, 사전등록자 가운데 참석이 확정된 등록자에게 별도의 ‘참석확정 메일’이 발송되며, 해당 메일을 받은 등록자에 한해 행사 참석이 가능하다.

참석자에게는 점심 식사가 제공되며, 세션 종료까지 참여한 참석자에게는 올리브영 기프트카드 3만원권을 웰컴 기프트로 증정한다.

행사 마지막에는 아이패드 에어 11인치, 애플워치 SE 3, 갤럭시 버즈4 등을 증정하는 경품 추첨도 진행된다.

사전등록은 앤앤에스피 공식 행사 페이지에서 진행할 수 있으며, 행사 관련 문의는 이메일(sales@nnsp.co.kr)로 하면 된다.

items.content:
Threat actors have been observed attempting to exploit a high-severity security flaw in WordPress Core shortly after patches were released.

The vulnerability, which does not have a CVE identifier, relates to a case of remote code execution impacting WordPress Core versions 4.7 through 7.1.3. It carries a CVSS score of 8.1 on the CVSS scoring system. Patches for the flaw were released on October 28, 2026.

"This is due to predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core upgrades," Wordfence said . "This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server during the upgrade window."

The WordPress security company noted that successful exploitation requires an "attacker to hit a very narrow window while WordPress is unpacking a complete Core update."

The issue boils down to the fact that affected versions unpack new files part of a full-package Core update into a predictable directory under "wp-content/upgrade." This copy also includes the WordPress installer.

"Because the staging directory is web-accessible on many servers, an unauthenticated attacker who requests the installer at precisely the right moment can interact with the staged WordPress copy and progress to PHP code execution," Alex Thomas, who leads the Wordfence Threat Response Team, said.

A threat actor who is able to win the race condition can gain the ability to execute code on the server, assuming the following conditions are met -

Although that window has been observed to last only seconds in normal lab environments, threat actors are polling vulnerable paths, such as "setup-config.php," repeatedly in an attempt to trigger the flaw. Over the past 24 hours, Wordfence said it has blocked 62,969 attacks targeting the vulnerability.

"Two of the largest sources repeatedly polled small groups of sites for roughly 14.5 hours, behavior consistent with trying to catch the brief upgrade window," Thomas said. "Other sources tested many staging-directory and version-name variations."

"Not every request used the exact vulnerable path, but the sustained polling and exact-layout probes show that attackers quickly understood the race condition and began targeting it."

With active exploitation attempts already underway, WordPress site owners are advised to update to version 7.1.4 as soon as possible and look for suspicious requests to PHP files located under "wp-content/upgrade," as well as unfamiliar administrator accounts, plugins, or PHP files.

items.content:
SS7 and Diameter Attacks: How Signaling Flaws Expose Your Phone

SS7 and Diameter signaling attacks can track, intercept, and impersonate you. Here’s how they work and how to stop them.

Your phone can be tracked, your SMS two-factor codes can be intercepted, and your number can be impersonated, all without malware, a phishing link, or any access to your device.

The attacks happen inside the telecom network, in the carrier-to-carrier control protocols known as signaling, the automated descendants of the old telephone switchboard. Most users never see them, and most carriers can’t reliably stop them.

Signaling attacks aren’t new. Most recently, they made headlines when Iranian-linked actors reportedly exploited outdated network technology to locate the phones of US personnel in the Middle East during the Iran war.

But the vulnerability has been around for decades, and it’s been used for far more everyday crimes, like intercepting bank one-time passcodes. It has even been demonstrated by popular YouTubers: Veritasium hijacked a tech influencer’s calls and texts using only his phone number.

Criminals have reportedly exploited signaling protocols in attacks on bank accounts and global telecom infrastructure.

Citizen Lab exposed two long-running commercial surveillance campaigns abusing SS7 and Diameter, with thousands of attacks against targets in dozens of countries.

Congressman Ted Lieu’s phone was hacked on live TV via SS7 on 60 Minutes Australia

Attackers have intercepted SMS one-time passcodes to drain victims’ bank accounts.

Every call, text, and mobile data session requires your carrier to verify you’re a paying customer and route your traffic to the right destination.

Carriers do this with signaling–background messages that identify your location and forward traffic accordingly. Signaling has been the connective tissue between global providers for decades, and it is one of the most overlooked attack surfaces in mobile security.

Two protocols do most of the work: SS7 (from the 1970s, used in 2G/3G) and Diameter (its successor, used in 4G and most 5G).

Both were designed when a small number of large operators could plug into the system, so they assume that traffic claiming to come from a legitimate operator really does. SS7 has essentially no process for authenticating the machine making a request.

Diameter supports stronger authentication on paper, but operators don’t always deploy basic protections like encryption, and many fall back on the same peer-to-peer trust model.

An attacker with access to the global signaling backbone, through a commercial leasing arrangement or a compromised operator, can send messages that carriers worldwide treat as trustworthy.

Signaling lets an attacker ask your carrier questions and make claims on your behalf:

Harvest your IMSI. Knowing your number, an attacker can request your International Mobile Subscriber ID (IMSI) under the pretense of routing a call or SMS. It can be reused for follow-on attacks for years.

Locate you in real time. Queries can return the cell tower you last connected to. Others, normally reserved for emergency responders, can return the actual coordinates your phone reports.

Intercept communications. The attacker claims you’ve roamed onto another network, so your calls and texts are redirected to them. Combined with a stolen username and password, this delivers your SMS second factor to the attacker instead of you.

Impersonate or block you. With your IMSI, an attacker can place calls or send SMS as you. A false roaming claim can also cut off service to your phone.

Disrupt networks. Deliberately misconfigured signaling messages can overwhelm provider systems.

None of this touches your device. It happens in automated transactions you can’t see and that leave no trace on your phone.

items.title: Passkeys Are Better Than Passwords. But They Are Not Enough.
items.summary: As organizations eliminate passwords, attackers will adapt. Instead of attacking the authenticator directly, they will look for opportunities around it. The post Passkeys Are Better Than Passwords. But They Are Not Enough. appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
For decades, passwords have been one of cybersecurity’s most persistent weaknesses. Users forget them, reuse them, share them, and surrender them to convincing phishing sites. Attackers steal credentials, automate credential stuffing, and increasingly use artificial intelligence to make social engineering more effective.

Passkeys promise to eliminate much of this problem.

Built on public-key cryptography, passkeys replace shared secrets with cryptographic credentials. There is no password for an attacker to steal, intercept through phishing, or reuse against another service. Properly implemented passkeys are also phishing-resistant because authentication is bound to the legitimate service.

That represents a significant improvement over passwords and many traditional forms of multi-factor authentication (MFA). But it does not answer a more fundamental question: Just because someone successfully authenticated, should we continue to trust that identity ?

Passkeys strengthen authentication. They do not eliminate identity risk.

Traditional authentication frequently relies on passwords combined with one-time passcodes, SMS messages, or push notifications. While stronger than passwords alone, these methods remain vulnerable to phishing, adversary-in-the-middle attacks, MFA fatigue, SIM swapping , and social engineering. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Passkeys fundamentally change that model. Instead of presenting a reusable secret, the user’s device holds a private cryptographic key while the service retains the corresponding public key. The private key is not transmitted during authentication.

This provides meaningful protection against phishing, credential stuffing, password database theft, and other attacks built around stealing reusable credentials. Passkeys can also improve usability because users no longer need to remember complex passwords or repeatedly retrieve authentication codes.

Organizations should welcome that transition. The mistake would be assuming that stronger authentication solves the broader identity security problem though.

When passkey authentication succeeds, the system has strong cryptographic evidence that a credential associated with an account completed the authentication process.

But was the account legitimately established? Has the underlying identity been compromised? Is the device trustworthy? Is an attacker operating through an authenticated session?

A perfectly functioning authentication mechanism cannot compensate for an identity that should never have been trusted.

If an attacker establishes or takes control of an account before a passkey is bound to it, the organization may subsequently perform highly secure authentication of the wrong person. The stronger the authenticator becomes, the more important the integrity of enrollment becomes.

Legitimate users also do not always authenticate from the same device. Phones are lost, stolen, damaged, or replaced. Employees receive new laptops. Consumers switch technology ecosystems.

Passkey synchronization addresses many of these scenarios by making credentials available across supported devices. But organizations still need to accommodate legitimate users who arrive without access to the expected passkey.

At that point, the challenge shifts from authentication to recovery and re-establishing trust. How does the organization determine whether someone requesting access from an unfamiliar device is the legitimate account owner?

If the fallback relies on a password, SMS code, email link, knowledge-based question, or help desk process, attackers may target that weaker recovery path.

The passkey has not been compromised. The attacker has gone around it.

Organizations therefore need a secure way to re-establish identity trust before associating a new authenticator or device with an existing account.

items.content:
두산 디지털이노베이션BU(DDI)가 미국 국방부 사이버 보안 인증(CMMC) 컨설팅 기관 자격을 취득하고 국내 기업의 미국 방산 공급망 진출 지원에 나선다.

DDI는 CMMC의 공식 인정기구인 사이버 AB(The Cyber AB)로부터 컨설팅 기관(RPO) 자격을 취득했다고 밝혔다. CMMC는 미국 방산 공급망에 참여하는 기업의 사이버 보안 역량을 의무적으로 평가·인증하는 제도로, 핵심 기술 데이터 유출을 방지하기 위해 도입되어 단계적으로 적용되고 있다.

RPO는 기업이 CMMC 요건을 충족하도록 준비 과정과 개선 활동을 지원하는 공식 기관이다. DDI는 CMMC 등록 실무자(RP) 자격을 보유한 전문 인력과 글로벌 IT 인프라 운영 경험을 바탕으로 요구사항 진단, 보안 체계 개선, 평가 증적 준비, 제3자 평가 대응까지 전 과정을 지원한다.

DDI는 자격 취득 과정에서 중앙대학교 산업보안학과 및 보안대학원과 협력해 CMMC 컨설팅 방법론을 공동 개발했다. 해당 방법론은 프로젝트 착수 및 범위 정의, 보안 요구사항 진단과 갭(GAP) 분석, 보안 통제 구현, 증적 확보 및 모의평가, 평가 대응 및 사후 관리 단계로 구성된다.

DDI 이정환 전무는 "미국 방산 공급망에 참여하려는 국내 기업에 CMMC는 꾸준히 준비해야 할 보안 기준"이라며 "기업별 환경을 정확히 진단해 과제를 제시하고 인증 이후에도 자체 보안 관리 역량을 갖추도록 지원하겠다"고 밝혔다.

items.content:
인증 없이 원격에서 시스템 제어권을 탈취할 수 있는 보안 취약점 'PHP2Shell'과 관련해 외부 웹서버보다 기업 내부망에 숨어 있는 장비의 보안 위협이 더 심각하다는 분석 결과가 나왔다.

지니언스는 인터넷 접점이나 내부망에 연결된 NAS, 공유기 등 네트워크 장비와 방화벽이 사이버 공격의 다음 타깃이 될 가능성이 높다고 경고하며 기업들의 선제적 조치를 촉구했다.

PHP2Shell 취약점은 지난 10월 미국 사이버안보·인프라보안국(CISA)의 알려진 악용 취약점 목록에 등재됐다. 공격자들은 내부 사설 IP 대역의 취약 장비를 장악한 뒤 내부 침투 확산의 교두보로 삼거나 랜섬웨어를 유포하고 있다.

지니언스가 클라우드 NAC 플랫폼에 연동된 장비 식별 데이터를 분석한 결과, 내부망에서 PHP 환경을 구동 중인 장비 중 96%가 PHP2Shell 취약점에 노출된 것으로 확인됐다. 취약 장비 중 78%는 PHP 공식 지원이 중단된 8.1 이하 구버전이었으며, 2018년에 지원이 종료된 5.x 이하 버전을 구동 중인 장비도 48%에 달했다.

장비 구성은 전통적인 서버가 24%에 불과했고, CCTV와 보안 솔루션 등 IoT 기기가 17%, 미확인 자산이 27%를 차지했다. 확인된 장비의 89%는 외부 인터넷 검색엔진으로 접근이 불가능한 내부망 사설 IP 대역에 위치해 있었다. 관리자가 내부에 PHP가 탑재된 사실을 인지하지 못해 장기간 방치되는 구조적 문제를 안고 있다.

지니언스는 외부 스캔 툴에 의존해 IP를 대입하는 방식으로는 내부망 사각지대를 찾을 수 없으며, 내부망 전체 자산의 정확한 가시성 확보가 선행되어야 한다고 설명했다. 제조사 지원이 종료되어 패치가 없는 구형 장비는 교체 전까지 네트워크 접근을 즉시 차단하고 격리해야 한다.

지니언스는 지니안 NAC의 자산 식별 기술을 에이전틱 AI 기반으로 고도화하고 있다. 플랫폼의 핵심인 CAASM(Cyber Asset Attack Surface Management)을 통해 내부 IT 자산을 실시간 파악하고 통합 관리하며, AI 에이전트가 패치 정보와 취약점 동향을 스스로 분석해 내부망 공격 표면의 사각지대를 해소한다는 방침이다.

items.summary: It allowed customers to host hack-for-hire services, supported ransomware and infostealer operators, and accepted crypto payments. The post Bulletproof Host Virtualine Loses Its Domain to FBI Seizure appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.content:
The FBI has seized virtualine.net, the domain of a Russian-speaking bulletproof hosting services provider associated with various cybercriminal operations.

According to court documents, Virtualine, also known as Secury, Massgod, Spamhouse, Lanedo, and Omegatech, has been hosting customers’ illicit services and helped them evade law enforcement takedown attempts.

In posts on cybercrime forums, Virtualine promoted support for various types of cybercriminal activity, including phishing, spam, carding, and more; advertised its ability to move customer services to unaffiliated infrastructure; and claimed it intentionally ignored abuse.

It also allowed users to post and sell explicit images and videos of minors and adults, and supported at least one customer that offered a hack-for-hire service aimed at stealing sexually explicit content from online accounts.

Despite receiving numerous takedown requests from law enforcement agencies in several countries, Virtualine continued to aid the customer and even helped them create a new website for uploading the illicit content. The provider continues to host the new website.

According to blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs, Virtualine has been used, among others, by ransomware groups and an infostealer operator. Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

“Virtualine received more illicit-attributed cryptocurrency than any other TRM-labeled bulletproof hosting provider, despite receiving less total value than several peers,” the company says .

The bulletproof hosting provider first emerged on the cybercrime forum Exploit in 2024, but claims to have been operating since 2019. It claimed to have had the largest collection of autonomous system numbers for malware and botnet hosting in 2025.

Most of the payments Virtualine’s labeled Bitcoin addresses have received came from a Russian drug marketplace (44%) and a large sextortion scheme (17%). A cryptocurrency mixer accounted for 13% of them and ransomware for 5%. In 2026, Virtualine also received payments from the StealC infostealer operators.

“A domain seizure disrupts how customers find and access a service. It does not, by itself, establish that the operator has stopped working, or that customers have lost access to all underlying infrastructure,” TRM notes.

items.content:
피앤피시큐어는 오는 11월 12일 서울 여의도 콘래드 서울 호텔에서 열리는 금융정보보호 컨퍼런스 'FISCON 2026'에 참가해 'FaceLocker'를 활용한 화면정보 유출 방지와 안면인증 기반 업무시스템 연동 방안을 소개한다.

올해 20주년을 맞는 FISCON 2026은 'Now for Next Finance'를 주제로 AI로 재편될 미래 금융의 보안 전략을 모색하는 행사다. 피앤피시큐어는 이번 행사에서 금융회사 업무 환경에 적용할 수 있는 화면 보안과 사용자 인증 방안을 제시한다.

금융회사의 업무 화면에는 고객 개인정보와 거래정보를 비롯해 시스템 운영정보, 내부 검토 자료 등 다양한 중요정보가 표시된다. 최근 계정 탈취 위협이 빈번해지면서 ID와 PW 로그인을 넘어 실제 본인 여부를 철저히 검증하는 사용자 인증 방안이 필요하다. 로그인 이후에도 스마트폰 촬영이나 무단 열람 등 비주얼 해킹(Visual Hacking)으로 인한 화면 정보 유출 위협에 대비해야 한다.

FaceLocker는 비전 AI 기반 실시간 사용자 검증과 화면 촬영, 타인 접근, 사용자 자리비움 등의 위험 상황 탐지를 통해 화면정보 유출 가능성을 줄인다. 피앤피시큐어는 이를 바탕으로 고객정보와 내부 업무정보를 취급하는 금융 업무 환경의 화면 보안 강화 방안을 선보인다.

안면인증 기반 업무시스템 연동도 주요 기능이다. FaceLocker는 기존 SSO(Single Sign-On) 시스템 및 개별 서비스와의 인증 연계를 지원한다. 기업의 인증 체계와 연동해 안면인증을 업무시스템 접근 과정에 활용하고, 사용자 확인을 강화하면서 인증 과정의 편의성을 높인다.

피앤피시큐어는 이번 행사에서 두 기능의 활용 가치를 함께 전달한다. 업무시스템에 접속하는 단계에서는 안면인증 연계를 통해 사용자를 확인하고, 업무 수행 중에는 화면 촬영이나 타인 접근 등 정보 노출 위험에 대응한다. 이를 통해 금융회사 담당자들에게 접속부터 실제 화면 사용까지 이어지는 업무 보안 방안을 제안한다.

피앤피시큐어 김영수 금융사업부장은 "금융 업무의 보안은 시스템에 접속하는 사용자를 확인하는 것과 업무 중 중요정보가 노출되지 않도록 보호하는 것을 함께 고려해야 한다"며 "이번 FISCON에서 FaceLocker의 화면정보 유출 방지와 안면인증 기반 업무시스템 연동을 통해 보안성과 편의성을 함께 확보할 수 있는 방안을 소개하겠다"고 말했다.

items.content:
포티투닷은 대규모 언어 모델 기반 차량용 음성 AI 에이전트 '글레오 AI'에 고객 피드백을 반영한 첫 번째 무선 소프트웨어 업데이트(OTA)를 제공한다.

글레오 AI는 지난 5월 현대자동차 더 뉴 그랜저를 통해 처음 선보인 기술이다. 현대자동차의 플레오스 커넥트 OTA를 통해 진행되는 이번 업데이트는 내비게이션 검색, 전화, 문자 메시지 읽기 등 차량 내 자주 사용하는 기능의 개선에 초점을 맞췄다.

포티투닷은 글레오 AI와 내비게이션의 연계 검색 기능을 강화했다. 주행 중 원하는 장소를 음성으로 요청하면 LLM이 사용자의 의도와 맥락을 파악해 실제 주행 경로상 이용하기 편리한 장소를 검색한다. 휴게소, 주유소, 화장실 등 근거리 접근성이 중요한 장소는 별도의 조건을 말하지 않아도 현재 위치와 거리를 고려해 최적의 장소를 제안한다. 사용자는 내비게이션을 직접 조작하지 않고 음성 소통만으로 필요한 장소를 검색하고 목적지를 설정할 수 있다.

차량 내 커뮤니케이션 기능의 편의성과 안전성도 높였다. 음성 명령으로 문자메시지 읽기 기능을 실행하면 TTS 엔진이 메시지 내용을 읽어주는 온디바이스 기능을 새로 지원한다. 뒷좌석 탑승자의 음성 명령에 따른 전화 발신과 문자 전송을 제한해 의도하지 않은 기능 실행을 방지한다.

주유소 검색 시 유종별 가격 정보를 함께 제공하며, 경유지가 여러 곳일 경우 전체 장소의 정보와 잔여 시간을 글레오 AI를 통해 안내한다. 블루투스를 통한 음악 재생 실행 요청 시 연결 상태에 따라 오디오가 자연스럽게 재생되도록 로직을 개선했다.

글레오 AI 업데이트는 더 뉴 그랜저 차량을 대상으로 무선 배포를 시작한다. 플레오스 커넥트 최신 소프트웨어가 배포되면 차량 시동 시 표시되는 안내에 따라 서비스 센터 방문 없이 업데이트를 진행할 수 있다.
